## Trading Session Report

**Duration:** ~10 minutes of active trading (07:59 – 08:08 UTC)

### Trades Made
**25 trade fills** from my orders across 10 markets: NVDA, AAPL, 0700-HK (Tencent), ANT (Anthropic), NAURA, Biren Tech, SONY, GLD, QQQ, GOOGL, 1810-HK (Xiaomi), SPY.

### Profit & Loss
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Starting account value | $18.84 |
| Ending account value | $18.69 |
| **Net loss** | **-$0.15** |

### What Went Wrong

1. **Spread costs were the #1 killer.** Most markets had 0.2–0.5% bid-ask spreads. Entering at market means buying the ask and selling the bid — every round-trip cost ~0.3–0.5% in spread alone, wiping out any small directional gains on a $5 position. With ~$0.01–0.03 spread cost per trade and 12+ round-trips, spread alone accounts for most of the loss.

2. **Taker fees compounded the damage.** 0.045% taker fee on every entry and exit adds ~$0.0045 per round-trip. Total fees in my session: ~$0.05.

3. **Illiquidity trapped the best trade.** Biren Tech was up +$0.043 unrealized but had *zero bids* in the order book. Three market sell attempts failed before a resting limit order finally filled — and at a worse price ($2.08 vs mark $2.10).

4. **Scalping doesn't work at this frequency.** The bid-ask spread means you start every trade underwater. You need the market to move >0.5% in your favor just to break even. At 1–2 minute holding periods, that rarely happened.

### What I'd Do Differently
- Use limit orders (maker-only) to avoid the spread and pay lower fees (0.015% vs 0.045%)
- Hold positions longer to let trends develop beyond the spread cost
- Avoid illiquid names regardless of how attractive their momentum looks
- Trade fewer, higher-conviction positions instead of rapid rotation
